scenes.heading: JSON Format
scenes.subheading: The language of APIs and semi-structured data
scenes.narration: JSON, or JavaScript Object Notation, is a lightweight text format that represents data as nested objects and arrays.

scenes.heading: Why JSON is everywhere
bullets: Native to web APIs and JavaScript
scenes.narration: JSON is human-readable and self-describing because every value carries a labeled key. It supports nested objects and arrays, so it naturally represents hierarchical data. It is native to web APIs and JavaScript, which made it the default language of the modern web. And its flexible schema can evolve over time without breaking consumers.

scenes.heading: Working with JSON in Python
scenes.code:
import json

raw = '{"user": "Ada", "roles": ["admin", "editor"]}'
data = json.loads(raw)
print(data["user"])
print(data["roles"][0])
scenes.narration: Here we parse a JSON string into a Python object using json.loads. The result behaves like a dictionary, so we read the user field by key. Because roles is an array, we can index into it to get the first role. This ease of moving between text and nested structures is exactly why JSON dominates API communication.

scenes.heading: JSON vs CSV
scenes.narration: JSON can represent nested, hierarchical data and labels every value with a key. CSV can only represent flat rows and relies on a single header line for names. When your data has nesting or an evolving shape, JSON is the far better fit.

scenes.text: JSON is the go-to format for APIs and semi-structured data thanks to its flexibility and readability.
scenes.narration: The bottom line is that JSON's flexibility and readability make it the default choice for APIs and semi-structured data.
